dcp.name: zero-volume-box-origin-only
dcp.what: A caller asking read_box for an empty box away from the origin, such as rows [1,1), would receive elements_covered == elements_expected == 0 and complete=True, i.e. a 'complete' read that examined no data.

dcp.name: empty-dcp-accepted-when-blobs-exist
dcp.what: A DCP directory whose metadata contains only _extra_state byte blobs and zero tensors would open as a valid WeightSource with tensor_keys() == (), so a downstream all(...) over keys becomes the vacuous-truth pass from incident #6.
dcp.replacement: if not tensor_md and not nontensor:

dcp.name: float64-accumulator-downgraded
dcp.what: On huge-magnitude tensors the comparison would overflow/underflow back into the historic failure class and could again manufacture an impossible self-comparison (the 1.80-cosine incident) instead of an exactly reproducible cosine/RMS.

dcp.name: bitwise-self-check-only-for-zeros
dcp.what: Bitwise-identical nonzero tensors would no longer force the computed cosine to be exactly 1.0; a broken reduction could assert EXACT while its own cosine contradicts the bits, laundering bad numerics into a green report.

dcp.name: overlap-pair-scan-skips-neighbors
dcp.what: Two stored chunks that overlap adjacent regions could double-store rows while their volumes still sum to the declared size, so read_full/read_box would report exact coverage even though the written regions do not tile the tensor.
dcp.anchor:
for i in range(len(written)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(written)):
dcp.replacement:
for i in range(len(written)):
            for j in range(i + 2, len(written)):

dcp.name: orphan-chunk-treated-as-mere-hole
dcp.what: A tensor metadata chunk with no storage record would stop being reported as 'metadata declares a chunk that has no storage record'; operators would get a generic short-coverage error and lose the exact corruption that distinguishes orphaned metadata from a simple hole.

manifest.name: attempt-scan-loses-end-anchor
manifest.what: A run directory containing only lookalike files (attempt-0001.json.bak, half-named records) counts as having recorded attempts: the scanner trusts names that merely start with a valid prefix, so a stale backup file is read as manifest attempt 1 and attempt numbering silently skips over phantom slots.

manifest.name: corrupt-slot-silently-skipped
manifest.what: store.attempts() on a run whose only record is corrupt returns zero attempts, reading exactly like ''nothing ever ran'' — the corrupt slot vanishes from the record the way the 27 overwritten manifests did, and nothing ever raises.

manifest.name: save-uses-clobbering-replace
manifest.what: Saving a conflicting manifest over an existing attempt quietly rewrites history in place: the previous launch's record is destroyed and the slot shows only the newest claim — the exact overwrite that made 27 of 62 launches disappear, now succeeding without a sound.

manifest.name: identical-retry-always-raises
manifest.what: A crash-safe launcher that retries its manifest write always fails with ManifestExistsError: a byte-identical re-save of the same computation is reported as a slot conflict, so a rerun of a successful save looks like two different computations fighting over one attempt.

manifest.name: fingerprint-swallows-job-id
manifest.what: Two attempts of the same computation no longer fingerprint equally once they run under different scheduler jobs: requeues and relaunches always look like different mathematics, so 'same fingerprint, same computation' stops being checkable for anything that was ever resubmitted.

manifest.name: absent-key-compares-equal
manifest.what: differs_from short-circuits to 'equal' before reading a key that exists in only one manifest: a manifest missing OBJECTIVE_SWITCH compares identical to one that has it, so the 12/12 split disappears from the field-level diff — exactly the vacuous all([])-is-True the audit's own verifier shipped.
manifest.replacement: if False and key not in a:

manifest.name: unborn-head-reports-clean
manifest.what: A freshly git-init'ed repository with zero commits reports CaptureStatus.CLEAN — 'working tree matches the recorded commit' asserted against a commit that does not exist. Every capture on an empty repo reads as a verified clean checkout.
manifest.anchor:
if commit is None:
        # Unborn HEAD: the least reproducible state a repository can be in — there
        # is no commit to anchor the record against, and `git diff HEAD` is empty
        # by construction. It must never read as CLEAN.
        overall = CaptureStatus.NOT_CAPTURED
manifest.replacement:
if commit is None:
        # Unborn HEAD: the least reproducible state a repository can be in — there
        # is no commit to anchor the record against, and `git diff HEAD` is empty
        # by construction. It must never read as CLEAN.
        overall = CaptureStatus.CLEAN

manifest.name: latest-returns-first-attempt
manifest.what: require_manifest returns the oldest attempt of a run instead of the most recent: a relaunch whose manifest exists passes the gate while every consumer of 'the manifest that launched this run' is handed the first attempt's configuration and code claims, silently.
manifest.anchor:
all_attempts = self.attempts(run_id)
        if not all_attempts:
            raise ManifestMissing(f"no provenance manifests recorded for run {run_id!r}")
        return all_attempts[-1]
manifest.replacement:
all_attempts = self.attempts(run_id)
        if not all_attempts:
            raise ManifestMissing(f"no provenance manifests recorded for run {run_id!r}")
        return all_attempts[0]

topology.name: comparison-never-compares
topology.what: An entrypoint that silently forces cp=1 over the launcher's CP=4 is reported as 'the runtime honours the declared config' — declared_vs_effective always takes the match path, so a knob that appears configurable and is not gets a green check mark again.

topology.name: match-path-reports-agreement-without-coverage
topology.what: A matching comparison says 'the runtime honours the declared config' but omits how many fields were compared, so a full seven-field comparison is indistinguishable from a comparison that read nothing.

topology.name: mismatch-path-drops-coverage-summary
topology.what: When declared and effective disagree, the BLOCK findings name the differing fields but no finding ever states how many fields were compared — a partial comparison that happened to catch a difference looks identical to a full one.

topology.name: layout-fields-excluded-from-comparison
topology.what: declared_vs_effective silently skips nodes and gpus_per_node: a runtime that lands the job on a different node count or GPU-per-node count than the manifest declares passes as full agreement, and the coverage count no longer covers the layout.

topology.name: partition-normalization-keeps-spellings-distinct
topology.what: gpu-a100 and gpu_a100 are treated as two unrelated partitions, so the measured 188-files-one-way/4-the-other split on a single partition is reported as 'N distinct partitions, 0 spelling variants' — the exact estate failure reads as clean.

topology.name: empty-partition-scan-passes-vacuously
topology.what: A scan of zero files reports OK instead of BLOCK: supplying no corpus to partition_consistency returns a clean verdict, repeating the all([]) is True incident the check's own message claims to refuse.

topology.name: dash-p-flag-noise-becomes-partitions
topology.what: The sbatch/srun gating on the short '-p' form is dropped, so 'cp -p weights.bin' manufactures a partition named weights.bin and a corpus containing nothing but flag noise is reported partition-consistent — the not-found BLOCK that distinguishes real extraction from noise never fires.

parity.name: cosine-range-check-needs-both-impossible-directions
parity.what: A broken accumulator's cosine of 1.80 is reported as data again instead of raising — the exact 'tensor's cosine with itself printed as >1' incident this guard descends from. Since a finite cosine cannot simultaneously exceed 1.0+slack and fall below -1.0-slack, no value ever trips the impossible-value check.
parity.anchor:
cosine is not None
        and math.isfinite(cosine)
        and (cosine > 1.0 + _COSINE_SLACK or cosine < -1.0 - _COSINE_SLACK)
parity.replacement:
cosine is not None
        and math.isfinite(cosine)
        and (cosine > 1.0 + _COSINE_SLACK and cosine < -1.0 - _COSINE_SLACK)

parity.name: self-cosine-slack-widened-past-reality
parity.what: A reduction that scores a bitwise-identical tensor's cosine with itself at 0.4 — a mathematically impossible self-similarity and the signature of a statistics bug — sails through the sanity guard and is printed as fact, because a deviation must now exceed 1.5 to be called impossible.
parity.anchor:
elements > 0
        and cosine is not None
        and (math.isnan(cosine) or abs(cosine - 1.0) > _SELF_COSINE_SLACK)
parity.replacement:
elements > 0
        and cosine is not None
        and (math.isnan(cosine) or abs(cosine - 1.0) > 1.5)

parity.name: dtype-mismatch-no-longer-blocks
parity.what: A checkpoint exported with one tensor silently written at the wrong dtype passes the weight-parity gate: the mismatch is still noted in the skipped list, but it never becomes a blocking finding, so the gate's verdict reads ok while cast-around is exactly what an auditor must assume happened.

parity.name: unread-keys-counted-as-compared
parity.what: The report's compared_keys count includes dtype- and shape-mismatched keys that were never numerically read — the coverage number overstates what was actually examined, and a report can claim N compared keys while fewer than N comparisons ever happened.

parity.name: none-cosine-report-laundered-to-one
parity.what: A zero-element tensor, or a key where one side is all zeros, reports cosine 1.0 — a perfect-similarity score for a comparison where no similarity was measurable — instead of the null that tells the reader no cosine exists. Consumers of to_dict can no longer distinguish 'measured identical direction' from 'cosine undefined'.
parity.replacement:
mismatched_elements=cmp.mismatched_elements,
        max_abs_diff=cmp.max_abs_diff,
        cosine=cmp.cosine if cmp.cosine is not None else 1.0,
        rel_frob=rel_frob,

parity.name: vacuity-no-longer-declared
parity.what: A parity report over zero common keys — the literal all([]) shape of Incident #6 — no longer declares itself vacuous: is_vacuous is False, the rendered verdict skips the VACUOUS banner, and to_dict reports vacuous: false for a comparison that examined nothing. The gate's own vacuous branch becomes dead code.

parity.name: zero-reference-rel-frob-underreported
parity.what: A genuinely nonzero tensor compared against an all-zero reference reports rel_frob 0.0 — 'identical to the zero tensor' — instead of the inf that states the difference is unbounded relative to the reference. A scrubbed-to-zero or never-written reference tensor masquerades as a perfect match on the relative-difference axis.

parity.name: dtype-mismatch-disguised-as-value-difference
parity.what: A dtype mismatch is recorded as an ordinary numeric DIFFER finding, so consumers can no longer tell 'never numerically compared — possible silent cast' apart from 'compared and outside tolerance'. Every numeric statistic for that key still shows inf/None for zero compared elements, but under a status that claims a value judgement was made.

                    ParityStatus.DTYPE_MISMATCH,
                    shape_left,
                    shape_right,
                    dtype_left,
                    dtype_right,
                    tolerances,
                    reason,
                )
parity.replacement:
_metadata_entry(
                    key,
                    ParityStatus.DIFFER,
                    shape_left,

                    dtype_right,

                    reason,

parity.name: inert-control-must-pass
parity.what: MUST SURVIVE: a trailing comment changes no behaviour, so the suite MUST stay green. If the battery reports this killed, its attribution machinery is proven unsound and the whole run is void — exit 2.

checkpoint_gates.name: aliasing-records-unique-fqns-instead
checkpoint_gates.what: The aliasing signature is gone: a checkpoint where 128 (or 32) expert FQNs all resolve to one stored byte range passes the distinctness gate, because 'distinct FQNs' is being counted instead of 'distinct storages' — exactly the incident's 'all names present, count matches, every dtype correct' disguise.
checkpoint_gates.anchor: storages = {t.storage_id if t.storage_id is not None else t.fqn for t in members}

checkpoint_gates.name: shard-count-mismatch-reads-as-match
checkpoint_gates.what: A checkpoint holding 16 expert shards against 128 declared is reported as 'present at declared count', because the declared-vs-present comparison now only flags layouts whose shard count equals the declared count — the local-name save signature passes silently.

checkpoint_gates.name: byte-volume-deficit-tolerance-swallows-incident
checkpoint_gates.what: The 5.71-GB-where-45.70-GB-was-correct checkpoint passes the byte-volume gate: the deficit must now exceed 99.9% before anything fires, so the incident's metadata-visible 0.125 byte ratio re-greens.

checkpoint_gates.name: coverage-denominator-purely-decorative
checkpoint_gates.what: A context reporting 4 expert tensors against a declared expectation of 8 (or any number) is never flagged: the declared-count denominator written into every Coverage object can be half the truth and nothing in the gates or the bridge suite compares checked against expected.

checkpoint_gates.name: first-save-composite-ignores-blocking-subgates
checkpoint_gates.what: A corrupt first checkpoint whose distinctness, byte-volume and completeness gates all FAIL still leaves the composite reporting 'all hold at first save' — the composite aggregates verdicts but the blocking set is empty by construction, so save #1 is never stopped.
checkpoint_gates.anchor: blocking = [r for r in sub if r.blocking]
